text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- The Socialist government wants Portuguese firms to get involved in the Polish privatisation process.
- Sonae group should post consolidated net profit of 7.8 billion escudos in 1996, analysts tell the paper.
- Construction company Engil posted 610 million escudos profit in the first half of 1996, 4.1 percent more than the same period of 1995, informed sources tell the paper.
- Occupancy of state owned inns (pousadas) rose 7.50 percent between January and August 1996, compared to the same year-ago period.
- Employment Ministry plans to spend around 144 billion escudos on training in 1997, covering some 500,000 people.
- The establishment of Sonae's new retail bank Universo Banco Directo will be signed next week with a capital of five billion escudos.
- Wine company Sogrape offered six billion escudos to buy Quinta da Aveleda which controls 30 percent of the vinho verde (young wine) market.
- President Jorge Sampaio hopes the U.S. will take no further unilateral military action against Iraq. Prime Minister Antonio Guterres has openly supported the U.S. position.

- The mini-crisis in the Gulf should not affect Portugal. State oil company Petrogal is maintaining fuel reserves at the maximum level and does not expect to return to the market to buy crude until the end of September, spokesman Antonio Mocho tells the paper. However, fuel prices could rise in Portugal in the coming months.
